headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Test on Australian soil
summary: The Tigers dominate the Darwin Test, marking a monumental shift in their Test identity and earning global respect.
details: Bangladesh has achieved an extraordinary Test victory over Australia in Darwin, dominating almost every session of the match.
The win is seen as more than just a scorecard, representing a moment of collective achievement and national confidence for a country currently facing political and social uncertainty.
The team displayed immense discipline, composure, and patience, avoiding spectacular shots in favor of constructed partnerships and purposeful fielding.
Tanzid Hasan scored 101, marking the first Test century by a Bangladeshi player in Australia, a symbolic achievement in his second Test match.
The victory has drawn widespread praise and congratulations from the cricketing world, while Australian media has reacted with shock to the 'disaster' defeat.
For the Bangladeshi-Australian community, the win serves as a positive global message about the country's ambition, ingenuity, and resilience.

headline_marked: BB sets [[Tk 60,000 crore target for agri-credit]] in FY27
headline: BB sets Tk 60,000 crore target for agri-credit in FY27
summary: The central bank aims to boost farm production and contain inflation by increasing rural credit disbursement by 54% year-on-year.
details: Bangladesh Bank has set a target to disburse Tk 60,000 crore in agricultural and rural credit for the fiscal year 2026-27, a 54% increase over the previous year's target of Tk 39,000 crore.
The central bank aims to stimulate the rural economy, create employment, and increase national macroeconomic output by achieving self-reliance among the rural population.
This high target is intended to boost agricultural production, which the BB says is key to achieving economic growth and controlling inflation.
To ensure credit reaches genuine farmers, banks can identify them using certificates from local agricultural extension officers, fisheries and livestock officers, or government-issued farmer's cards.
The BB has also relaxed rules for group-based agricultural credit and expanded coverage to include fish fingerling production, duck and poultry chick production, and camel farming.
New regulations have been introduced for organic fertilizer production and updated crop production calendars and repayment schedules.
For fruits like banana, papaya, mango, lemon, guava, and litchi, the BB has fixed specific disbursement and harvest periods, with repayment timelines starting after the harvest.
caption:
Tk 60,000 crore for farmers! Bangladesh Bank hikes agri-credit target by 54% to fight inflation.

Bangladesh Bank has set a target to disburse Tk 60,000 crore in agricultural and rural credit for the fiscal year 2026-27, a 54% increase over the previous year's target of Tk 39,000 crore.

The central bank aims to stimulate the rural economy, create employment, and increase national macroeconomic output by achieving self-reliance among the rural population.

This high target is intended to boost agricultural production, which the BB says is key to achieving economic growth and controlling inflation.

To ensure credit reaches genuine farmers, banks can identify them using certificates from local agricultural extension officers, fisheries and livestock officers, or government-issued farmer's cards.

The BB has also relaxed rules for group-based agricultural credit and expanded coverage to include fish fingerling production, duck and poultry chick production, and camel farming.

New regulations have been introduced for organic fertilizer production and updated crop production calendars and repayment schedules.

For fruits like banana, papaya, mango, lemon, guava, and litchi, the BB has fixed specific disbursement and harvest periods, with repayment timelines starting after the harvest.
